descs.t: Benjamin Netanyahu pushed for a strike on Iran before Israel's election on Tuesday, but President Trump refused, CNN reports, and Israeli outlets say IDF Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir objected to the plan. CNN also reports Israel has suspended plans for more strikes on Iran in the immediate term. We walk through what is reported and what happens next.

Netanyahu says Israel has fresh intelligence that Iran will launch attacks to disrupt Tuesday's election, while reports say his army chief resisted a strike order and Trump said no. At the same time Trump issued a second endorsement of Netanyahu. We look at what this clash means for Israel's election and for pressure on the Iranian regime.

Netanyahu warns that Iran wants to disrupt Israel's election, and the fight over whether to strike the regime first has reached the top of Israel's army and President Trump. The Times of Israel and Haaretz carry the reports. We break down who said no, why, and what it means for the regime in Tehran.

intro.plain: Big news out of Israel. CNN says Netanyahu pushed for a strike on Iran before Tuesday's election and Trump refused. Israeli reports say the army chief, Eyal Zamir, objected too, and Israel has put further strikes on hold for now. Let's go through what is actually reported and what it means. Chat, should Israel have struck before the vote?
intro.mid: Netanyahu says Iran is planning attacks to disrupt Israel's election on Tuesday. Reports say he wanted to strike first, his army chief pushed back, and Trump said no, while also endorsing him a second time. Let's work out what this means for the election and for the regime. Chat, who do you think made the right call here?
intro.bold: Netanyahu says the regime in Tehran wants to disrupt Israel's election, and he wanted to hit it first. Reports say his army chief resisted and Trump said not now. So the regime gets a pause. Let's look at whether that pause helps anyone but Tehran. Chat, is holding back right now a mistake?

hook.plain: Netanyahu wanted to strike Iran before Tuesday's election. Trump refused, CNN says, and Israel's army chief objected. Here is what happened and what comes next.
hook.mid: Days before Israel votes, Netanyahu, his army chief and Trump split over a strike on Iran. Here is what that clash means for the election and for the regime.
hook.bold: Netanyahu says Iran wants to disrupt Israel's election. He wanted to hit the regime first, and he was told no. Here is who stopped it, and what it costs.

descs.t: Lula da Silva has won a fourth term as Brazil's president, beating Flávio Bolsonaro in the runoff with 51.76% of the vote at 99.8% counted, according to reports. Bolsonaro refuses to concede and says he will ask the courts to annul the result. We walk through the count, the comeback and what Bolsonaro is now asking for.

Brazil's runoff is over on paper, but Flávio Bolsonaro says he cannot recognise Lula's win and blames a late court decision on voting hours. Reports say he was ordered to surrender his passport a day later, and Brazil's currency reportedly fell sharply. We look at the court rulings, the annulment bid and what a fourth Lula term means for Brazil.

Lula has a fourth term and Brazil is split over how he got it. Bolsonaro's camp says the rules were changed mid vote and wants the result thrown out, while Bolsonaro himself is reportedly ordered to hand over his passport. We go through the claims, what the evidence shows so far, and why the fight over Brazil's courts matters far beyond Brazil.

intro.plain: Brazil has a result. Lula da Silva beat Flávio Bolsonaro in the runoff and wins a fourth term, with reports putting him at 51.76% with almost every vote counted. Bolsonaro is refusing to concede and says he will ask the courts to annul it. So tell me in the chat: is this a fair win, or does Bolsonaro have a case?
intro.mid: Lula has won a fourth term in Brazil, and the fight started the same night. Flávio Bolsonaro says he cannot recognise the result, blames a late court decision on voting hours, and reports say he was then ordered to surrender his passport. That is a lot of court power in one election. Chat, would you trust this result?
intro.bold: Lula wins Brazil again, and his opponent says the rules were changed while people were still voting. Flávio Bolsonaro wants the whole thing annulled, and a day later reports say he was told to hand over his passport. When the courts decide this much, people stop trusting elections. So chat, stolen or sour grapes?

hook.plain: Lula da Silva has won a fourth term in Brazil, and the man he beat refuses to accept it. Here is how the count went and what Flávio Bolsonaro is now asking the courts to do.
hook.mid: A late ruling on voting hours, an annulment bid and a passport order, all in two days. Here is what happened after Brazil's runoff, and why the courts are now the story.
hook.bold: Brazil's loser says the rules changed mid vote, and a day later he is reportedly told to give up his passport. Here is the case on both sides, and what it means for Brazil.
